findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the exact pipx invocation and version that produced the 'pipx needs uv>=0.9.17' error (was `--cooldown` involved, either explicitly or via a global pipx config?), and scope the README callout's conditional to the confirmed trigger rather than asserting it fires on all plain `pipx install` runs with uv<0.9.17.
evidence: Official pipx docs state: '--cooldown DAYS maps to uv's --exclude-newer P{DAYS}D. Relative cooldowns need uv 0.9.17 or newer.' — this scopes the uv>=0.9.17 requirement to --cooldown, not to all installs.
Plan asserts the failure occurs for 'A rebar client installing from source' via plain `pipx install "<path>[agents]"` with no mention of --cooldown being involved.

If the error is triggered by a pipx config-level cooldown default or a specific pipx version's behavior, the callout's conditional phrasing ('if you see this error') may still be useful — but the causal explanation in Context is unverified and will be reproduced in the README.
findings.finding: The plan's causal narrative — that a plain `pipx install "<path>[agents]"` fails with 'pipx needs uv>=0.9.17' when host uv is 0.7.18 — is not verified against actual pipx behavior. Per official pipx documentation, the uv>=0.9.17 minimum is scoped to the `--cooldown DAYS` feature (relative duration support), not to plain package installation. A bare `pipx install` without `--cooldown` should not trigger this error on uv 0.7.18. Baking this unverified trigger into AC1 (`grep -Fq "uv>=0.9.17" README.md`) and into the callout's conditional framing risks permanently documenting a false or overly broad error condition in the README.
findings.location: Context section ('Their pipx invocation reported that pipx needs uv>=0.9.17 while the selected host uv was 0.7.18') and AC1 (`grep -Fq "uv>=0.9.17" README.md`)
scenarios: A reader with uv 0.7.18 does a plain `pipx install nava-rebar` without --cooldown and does NOT see the error — the README callout now creates false alarm and confusion.
A user who DOES see the error has a pipx config with `cooldown` set globally, which the callout doesn't mention, making the actual fix (remove the global cooldown config, or upgrade uv) invisible.
findings.suggested_fix: Phrase the callout as: 'If you see `error: pipx needs uv>=0.9.17` — typically triggered when pipx is configured with a global `--cooldown` value and your host uv is older — use `pipx install --backend pip "<path>[agents]"` as a workaround. This is a host toolchain constraint, not a rebar packaging defect.'
